title: Label test-only failures separately from production reachability
applies_when: A native unit test changes package defaults or enables an internal feature, while a proposed cleanup or correctness defect is being judged for production delivery.
lesson: Inspect test initialization as well as production defaults. Run an external public client without test-only initialization, and separately test the internal failure mechanism with explicit scope. At the cited fsnotify revision, production enableRecurse is false but fsnotify_test.go init enables it. Default public calls are nonrecursive. The internal recursive Remove can still leave a live kernel watch after an invalidated descriptor causes an early error return and all Go mappings are cleared. Pair ordinary cleanup, invalid-only and mixed-live/stale controls; observe the actual resource, not only an empty bookkeeping map or an expected event. Here own fdinfo distinguishes EINVAL with no leftover from EINVAL with a remaining watch until Close. Record both results rather than blanket-rejecting an internal defect or calling it a default-production bug.
avoid_when: Internal helpers and unreleased features can have genuine bugs; lack of a default caller is not universal no-bug proof. A native internal result is not automatic PR eligibility or maintainer agreement. This observation is Linux inotify/Go1.25.10 at one revision, not all races, unexpected-event delivery, permanent OS leakage or other backends. The reproduction parks a real event reader; inability to establish that state is inconclusive, not a reason to inject an error and claim the same result. This development case is no longer an unseen evaluation sample and establishes no general Scout benefit.

evidence.note: Production recursion flag is unexported and false; recursivePath explicitly documents test-only enablement. Source gate, not a verdict about all internal cleanup.
The package test init enables recursion. A passing native unit baseline does not establish the default application's dispatch.

removePath clears Go mappings before kernel removal; normal watches return one descriptor, recursive watches can return several. The later loop's early return alone does not establish public reachability.

Sanitized independent external-client and internal native probes, with bounded attempts, actual kernel/cache controls and a small scoped observation. No target-project fix or full private log is published.
